children.text: For first-time travellers to Egypt, 12 days is a very workable length. You can stand at the entry of ancient Egypt at
Cairo
and
Giza
, see temples and royal tombs deeply at
Luxor
, and touch the southern Nile landscape at
Aswan
and
Abu Simbel

12 days doesn't mean "you can include everything." Egypt has long transfer distances, with heat, traffic, early starts, and walking time at sites greatly affecting trip stamina. A good itinerary thinks not only of listing sights but of where to rest and where to cut transfer.
Who this itinerary suits
This 12-day itinerary suits first-time visitors to Egypt who want to see major ancient sites properly. Centred on the pyramids, Cairo museum, Luxor's
Valley of the Kings
, Karnak, Aswan, and Abu Simbel, with a Nile cruise or Red Sea stay added if needed.

Not for those who want to pack sites while moving long daily. Egypt's appeal isn't only site count — morning light, Nile-side time, town walking, and conversation with guides matter too. Leaving margin makes the trip stay in memory more.
Base approach
For a first 12 days, narrowing the trip axis to Cairo, Luxor, and Aswan is stable. Cairo for Giza and museum, Luxor for east and west banks, Aswan for Philae and Abu Simbel.
For domestic transfer, flights work if time first. Luxor to Aswan can also go by land seeing
Edfu
and
Kom Ombo
, or by Nile cruise over several days. Not one right answer — choose by trip pace.

The Grand Egyptian Museum, sites, domestic flights, visa, and entry conditions can change. Confirm specific prices, opening range, and ticketing before booking and before departure on official sources or trusted operators.
Day 1: Arrive in Cairo
Don't pack sightseeing on arrival day. After long flights, immigration, baggage, and airport-to-city transfer take time.
After the hotel, light dinner nearby; prepare for Giza tomorrow. With stamina left, a short walk along the Nile or around Zamalek suffices. Pushing day one leaves fatigue into the following days.
Day 2: Giza pyramids and the Sphinx
Day two visits Giza as the first major peak. The three great pyramids of Khufu, Khafre, and Menkaure, the Sphinx, and viewpoints — head out early morning if possible.
Giza is wider than photos suggest and the sun feels strong. Decide in advance whether to enter the pyramid, use camel or carriage, and how far to walk; on-site decisions become easier.

Afternoon — museum or hotel rest by stamina. For the Grand Egyptian Museum, confirm display range, ticket, and entry method in advance. Giza, the museum, and Saqqara on the same day is heavy for first-timers.
Day 3: Saqqara, Memphis, or Cairo city

Day three, adding Saqqara to deepen ancient Egypt changes how Giza reads. Saqqara's Step Pyramid is important for understanding the early stage of royal-tomb architecture. With Memphis, you touch the memory of the ancient capital.
To see town layers rather than sites, time at
Coptic Cairo
or the Islamic district. Churches, mosques, old gates, and markets feel Cairo's thickness beyond antiquity.
Keep the night lighter to prepare for tomorrow's transfer. Cairo traffic is hard to read; the day before an airport or station, hold margin.
Day 4: Move to Luxor
Day four, move Cairo to Luxor. To save time, flights are realistic. Some take the night train; comfort and time predictability split opinion.
Arriving Luxor, don't push to the west bank — stay east-bank calmly. Evening into night, visit
Luxor Temple
to see lit columns and courtyards comparatively quietly.
Luxor is smaller than Cairo with closer Nile feel. Rest early to prepare for tomorrow's sites.
Day 5: Valley of the Kings and west-bank sites
Day five tours Luxor's west bank. Valley of the Kings, Hatshepsut mortuary temple, and Colossi of Memnon as axis, adding
Medinet Habu
or nobles' tombs by stamina and interest.
In the Valley of the Kings, openable tombs and supplementary-ticket targets vary. For Tutankhamun's or Seti I's tomb especially, confirm latest on-site.
Each west-bank place is impressive; packing all into one day overwhelms with fatigue. In hot seasons especially, premise early start and midday rest.
Day 6: Karnak and Luxor margin

Day six gives time to Karnak. Karnak is less a single temple than a huge religious complex expanded over long periods. The Great Hypostyle Hall, sacred lake, obelisks, and surrounding smaller temples — even half a day can be short.
Afternoon — Luxor Museum, Nile-side walk, short felucca ride — quieter time arranges trip rhythm. Beyond sites, Luxor has beautiful morning and evening light.
You could fit west-bank leftovers here; if yesterday was heavy, don't push. Across 12 days, stamina allocation is itinerary quality.
Day 7: Luxor to Aswan
Day seven, Luxor to Aswan. By land, Edfu's Temple of Horus and Kom Ombo en route give the feel of moving north to south along the Nile.
Edfu is known as a well-preserved Ptolemaic temple; Kom Ombo as a double temple tied to the crocodile god Sobek and the falcon god Horus. Different character from Luxor or Aswan major sites.

For a Nile cruise, the thinking on this section shifts. Cruises combine transfer and lodging; stop times depend on the ship's schedule. For self-pacing with detail, private car; for lighter transfer load, cruise.
Day 8: Aswan and
Philae Temple
Day eight, see Aswan unhurried. Philae Temple is one of Aswan's central sights. The current temple is relocated to avoid submersion; the boat to the island is memorable too.
With time, combine
the Nubian Museum
, Elephantine Island, and the Unfinished Obelisk. In Aswan, rather than consume sites in sequence, hold time for Nile width, islands, granite, and southern-Egyptian air.
For Nubian villages, beyond photos and shopping, mind care for local living space. Confirm who guides, what is visited, animal handling, and photo permission.
Day 9: Abu Simbel
Day nine visits Abu Simbel. Distance south from Aswan often makes for an early start; stamina is used. Ramesses II's great temple and Nefertari's small temple are worth including in 12 days.

Abu Simbel makes you think of ancient power expression and modern conservation together. The temples were relocated through international cooperation to avoid Aswan High Dam submersion. Knowing that, meaning beyond a huge temple appears.
Afternoon back in Aswan, lighter is wise. With long transfer, no need to add big sightseeing this night.
Day 10: Return to Cairo, or head to the Red Sea

Day ten branches by trip purpose. To weigh sites and urban culture, return to Cairo and use remaining time in Cairo. Adding another museum, deeper Islamic district, or revisiting Giza supplements understanding.
To rest at sea, the Red Sea fits. Hurghada or Marsa Alam suit travellers for diving, snorkelling, or resort stay.

Including the Red Sea in 12 days needs cutting somewhere. Whether to thin Luxor or Aswan for the sea — judge by trip priority. For first Egypt centring on sites, leaving the Red Sea for another trip is natural too.
Day 11: A buffer day in Cairo
Day eleven, holding a buffer in Cairo is reassuring. Museums, the Islamic district, around Khan el-Khalili, or Coptic Cairo missed earlier — choose by stamina and interest.
Don't fill this day completely. Domestic-flight delays, condition, weather, traffic, shopping, places to revisit — unexpected adjustments come late in the trip.
Returning to Cairo the day before the last reduces missing the international flight. Connecting from Aswan or Luxor to international flights the same day is hard to time; consider carefully.
Day 12: Departure
Last day, head to the airport by flight time. For morning flights, focus on transfer without sightseeing. For evening or night, brief time near the hotel — a café, last shopping — fits.
Egyptian airport transfer time varies by hour and traffic. For international-flight days, head with margin.
If including a Nile cruise
Including a cruise, replacing the Luxor-Aswan or Aswan-Luxor segment is natural. A 3- or 4-night cruise covers Edfu, Kom Ombo, and around Aswan while moving.
Large cruise ships have full facilities and light transfer; sightseeing time depends on the ship's schedule. Dahabiyas are quieter and slower, with different schedule and price conditions.
When choosing, confirm boat atmosphere, food, port stops, guide quality, and which sites you actually visit. "Nile cruise" alone covers very different experiences.
If including the Red Sea
A Red Sea itinerary suits adding rest to a site-centred trip. Hurghada is easy access with many resort options; Marsa Alam is preferred by travellers who make the sea itself the purpose.
Adding the Red Sea increases transfer. Cairo, Luxor, Aswan, Abu Simbel plus Red Sea makes 12 days short on margin. Without two or more sea nights, weigh the transfer cost.
For first Egypt with serious site interest, judge the Red Sea less by "fit if possible" and more by "is resting at the sea the purpose."
Season and timing
Egypt travel feels very different by season. Autumn through spring is generally easier; summer becomes very hot. In Luxor, Aswan, and Abu Simbel especially, heat loads the itinerary.
Visiting hot months, premise early-morning sites, midday rest, and lighter evening plans. Pushing morning items into the afternoon drops focus and stamina.
For dress, weigh walking ease, sun protection, and care at religious sites and town walks. Outside fine dining and hotels, walking shoes and clothing covering shoulders and knees suit.
Common failures

Common 12-day failures include treating transfer days at the same intensity as sightseeing days. Domestic flights and long-distance transfers include airport movement, waiting, check-in, baggage, and traffic delays. Packing a big site on transfer day suddenly makes the trip painful.

Another: seeing too much of Luxor's west bank in one day. Cramming Valley of the Kings, Hatshepsut, Medinet Habu, nobles' tombs, and the Valley of the Queens at once thins impression. Narrow target and walking with explanation stays deeper.
In Cairo too, avoid building Giza, Saqqara, multiple museums, and markets into the same day. With traffic and heat, map distance alone doesn't judge.
What to value in 12 days

12 days in Egypt isn't only time for efficient site touring. Seeing pyramids, going back in time at Saqqara the next day, entering the quiet of royal tombs at Luxor, and feeling the Nile landscape change at Aswan. That connection makes the trip more than a sequence of sightseeing.

For first travellers, prioritise seeing major places in good condition, even with slightly reduced plans. A 12-day Egypt itinerary doesn't get richer by packing — its real strength shows when sights and rest balance.

deck: Travelling Egypt in 12 days, centred on Cairo, Giza, Luxor, Aswan, and Abu Simbel — how to balance transfer and rest. A realistic build for first-time travellers.
